{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The red deer (\"Cervus elaphus\") is one of the largest deer species.","title":"Red deer"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" The red deer inhabits most of Europe, the Caucasus Mountains region, Asia Minor, Iran, parts of western Asia, and central Asia.","title":"Red deer"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" It also inhabits the Atlas Mountains region between Morocco and Tunisia in northwestern Africa, being the only species of deer to inhabit Africa.","title":"Red deer"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Red deer have been introduced to other areas, including Australia, New Zealand, United States, Canada, Peru, Uruguay, Chile and Argentina.","title":"Red deer"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" In many parts of the world, the meat (venison) from red deer is used as a food source.","title":"Red deer"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"The Forests of Mara and Mondrem were adjacent medieval forests in Cheshire, England, which in the 11th century extended to over 60 sqmi , stretching from the Mersey in the north almost to Nantwich in the south, and from the Gowy in the west to the Weaver in the east.","title":"Forests of Mara and Mondrem"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" Mara and Mondrem were a hunting forest of the Norman Earls of Chester, established soon after 1071 by the first earl, Hugh d'Avranches.","title":"Forests of Mara and Mondrem"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" They might earlier have been an Anglo-Saxon hunting forest.","title":"Forests of Mara and Mondrem"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Game included wild boar, and red, fallow and roe deer.","title":"Forests of Mara and Mondrem"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":"Europe, the Caucasus, Asia Minor, Iran, western and central Asia, the Atlas Mountains of north‑western Africa, and introduced populations in Australia, New Zealand, the United States, Canada, Peru, Uruguay, Chile and Argentina.","question":"What are some other areas that share a common deer species with the forests of Mara and Mondrem?"}
